previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for a two-week history of watery diarrhea and generalized malaise. She has a complex medical history including chronic graft-versus-host disease, prior stem cell transplant, diabetes, and recent T11 compression fracture. Stool studies were negative for infectious causes, and diarrhea improved during the hospital stay. The metoclopramide dose was reduced, and she was evaluated by GI for possible small intestinal bacterial overgrowth, though rifaximin was denied by insurance. Her sirolimus dose was decreased due to elevated levels, and she remained stable on anticoagulation for a right peroneal vein thrombus. Anemia and orthostatic hypotension were managed supportively. She was discharged home with plans for outpatient follow-up, sirolimus level monitoring, and repeat MRCP in six months for pancreatic cysts.

HISTORY:  ___ female has a history myeloblastic CML status post
transplant ___, chronic graft-versus-host disease of liver and eyes, also
history of DVTs on enoxaparin, admitted here for nausea, vomiting, diarrhea. 
Stable x 1 day on floor.  Liver graft-versus-host disease never evaluated by
biopsy (had previously incorrectly carried diagnosis of gut graft versus host
disease, before ruled out by gut biopsy).  While inpatient, want to rule out
liver graft-versus-host disease to reduce immunosuppressive medications
contributing to long-term morbidity (history of compression fracture). 
Hepatology recommends ultrasound-guided biopsy. ? Hepatic graft versus host
disease.  

TECHNIQUE:  Ultrasound-guided non-targeted liver biopsy.

FINDINGS AND PROCEDURE:

Procedure including risks, benefits and alternatives were explained to the
patient and after a detailed discussion through a ___ interpreter, 
informed written consent was obtained from the patient.  A time-out was
performed using 3 patient identifiers prior to the procedure.  

Nursing was present throughout the entire procedure.   Moderate sedation was
provided by administering divided doses of Fentanyl / Versed throughout the
total intra-service time of 10 min during which the patient's hemodynamic
parameters were continuously monitored.  1 mg of Versed and 100 mcg of
Fentanyl were administered during the procedure.  

The skin was marked with a marker.  The patient was prepped and draped in the
usual sterile fashion.  15 cc of lidocaine were used for local anesthesia. 
Under ultrasound guidance a 16 gauge core needle biopsy gun was used to
perform a non-targeted liver biopsy x 2 passes via a right intercostal
approach.   The samples were sent to pathology.  The procedure was well
tolerated.  There were no immediate post-procedural complications. 

Postoperative orders were entered into the order entry system for the patient
online.  

The attending radiologist, Dr. ___, was present for the entire procedure.  

IMPRESSION:

Non-targeted liver biopsy.  2 specimens sent to pathology.  No immediate
post-procedural complications.

with Dr. ___ on ___ at 10:30 AM.
